verdict: Visual pass with disclosed limitations: dark-slate clothing, sampled layout/CTA separation, recognizable forward/reverse pose progression and visible reduced-motion poster. No image-supported blocking material defect. Athlete realism remains a non-blocking art-direction concern, not evidence of broken rendering or rigging.

findings.result: Across original desktop start/mid/top/reverse, mobile mid, updated desktop captures and visible poster, shirt is dark blue-slate and trousers blue-gray slate—not white fallback. Skin, brown hair, dark shoes and pale chalk bag are distinct. Rounded hair and segmented, smooth limbs read as a stylized figurine. This is an art-direction preference relative to the document's tactile/editorial character, not a demonstrated material failure.

Original mid/reverse show the same recognizable raised-hand, spread-leg pose at different board perspectives. Updated video frames at 10s show lower/mid-board reaching, 15s show upper-board straddle, and 20s show descent to the lower board. Updated reverse-zero still restores the initial low crouched pose. No visible exploded joints or inverted anatomy in inspected samples. Summit legs are nearly horizontal in an exaggerated straddle; a more asymmetric loaded-leg stance would improve athletic realism, but these images do not establish impossible contact or a blocking rig defect.

Board, support feet and athlete fit in original desktop start/mid/top/reverse and mobile mid, with clear separation from copy/actions. Updated desktop start/ascent/reverse-zero preserve this separation. Both footer captures show the board gone and account actions unobstructed. Text cut by the top/bottom viewport during intermediate scroll captures is not evidence of container clipping.

Clear display-serif/sans hierarchy, dark surfaces and indigo primary actions broadly match the design document. Original mobile start stacks hero copy and actions without visible horizontal clipping; header controls fit. Mobile footer keeps Create free account/Sign in together and moves Open Boarded below. Small gray metadata is noticeably faint and tightly wrapped, especially Birch ply/specifications, but body copy and CTAs remain readable. Mobile start puts the illustration below the first fold; mobile mid has substantial negative space around the board.

Original mobile-reduced capture exposed only a tiny poster edge and could not approve composition. Updated resume-landing-32eb-reduced-poster.png closes that gap: whole board, feet and dark-clothed athlete are visible, contained, and separate from specifications/captions. Poster is brighter/paler than WebGL but clothing remains slate. Manifest records static state and zero canvases; image alone does not verify absence of GLTF loading/RAF or temporal stillness.

Red '1 Issue' badge remains visible in supplied original and updated images/video frames and sometimes overlays lower-left text. Main identifies unrelated walls inventory401 and documents an empty-array GET fixture; I did not independently diagnose it. This is capture contamination, not an image-supported athlete/landing defect.

inspected_files.video_inspection: Read six-frame preview plus full-resolution timestamp frames at 10s,15s,20s,28s. This is sampled rendered-video inspection, not uninterrupted playback or every-frame analysis.

limitations: Original evidence comprises eight WebGL-state screenshots and one reduced-motion static screenshot, not nine WebGL renders.

Updated landing identity differs from original; updated evidence supplements rather than silently replaces the original review. Fresh updated mobile animated reflow is not supplied; original mobile evidence remains the basis for that finding.
No numeric hand/foot contact, penetration, temporal smoothness or frame-perfect reversal claims. Sampled video supports progression and return, not every transition.
Only supplied dark desktop1440×1024/mobile390×844 surfaces reviewed; no zoom, intermediate widths, keyboard navigation, production asset delivery or actual link behavior validated.
Asset interception and unrelated GET fixture are manifest/Main-provided scope facts, not visually provable provenance.
